analysis:
The changed files are test-only: EngineV2BridgeTests.swift and NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift under provider-swift/Tests. Production code is not modified, so no production attack surface changes. The test changes add a decodeTable to a stub tokenizer and a stopStringScope parameter to the makeBridge helper. They also add tests for scoped stop-sequence reporting (matchedStopSequence) and for native-block requests carrying no stop scope.

The shown test context covers shared-KV-budget accounting, reservation release on rejection, teardown and shutdown, and SSD prefix-cache staging. It also covers lookup-receipt terminal coverage, seeded-ID isolation of receipt callbacks across scopes, and paged-KV capacity. These relate to T-041 (prefix cache), T-010 and T-029 (availability). The tests assert existing behavior: cache scope isolation (scope-a and scope-b callbacks stay separate), reservation release, and zero SSD bytes after rejection. They do not weaken any mitigation. The tests use temporary directories and in-memory keys (SymmetricKey(size: .bits256)), with no secrets or real KEK use.

I could not see the full patch of NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift (the excerpt is truncated) or the production implementation of matchedStopSequence and the native block stop-scope behavior. The production change that motivated these tests lies outside this batch. A later pass should verify that behavior if it is in scope. No security regression is identifiable from the test-only changes visible here.
